title: Decoupling Snapshot Publication from Staleness Tolerance in Distributed GRPO via Lossless Sparse Patches

contributions.purpose: Diagnoses the root cause of training instability in distributed GRPO under ECHO-2's staleness budget mechanism.
contributions.mechanism: Identifies that instability is driven by the publication period kappa (coupled as kappa = S - 1 in ECHO-2), not the staleness budget S, and proposes decoupling the two parameters.
contributions.evaluation: Supported by ECHO-2's reported instability at S = 11 and by the paper's off-policy divergence analysis.
contributions.source_quote: We identify that training instability in distributed GRPO is caused by the publication period kappa, not the staleness budget S, and propose decoupling these parameters to achieve both stability and worker tolerance.

contributions.purpose: Enables per-step weight publication (kappa = 1) at low communication cost while keeping large staleness budgets for slow workers.
contributions.mechanism: Sparse patch dissemination transmits only changed parameters, exploiting the natural 90.7% sparsity of single-step weight updates (vs 64.3% for 10-step accumulated updates).
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 12.5x compression and 89.9% broadcast time reduction.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce sparse patch dissemination that exploits natural weight update sparsity to enable per-step publication with 12.5x compression and 89.9% broadcast time reduction.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrates that decoupled per-step publication prevents training collapse under sustained off-policy conditions.
contributions.mechanism: Multi-seed stability comparison against the ECHO-2-style coupled baseline under sustained off-policy conditions, measuring collapse and KL divergence.
contributions.evaluation: Baseline collapses in 3/3 seeds while the proposed approach remains stable in 3/3 seeds, with a 1400x reduction in KL divergence.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that under sustained off-policy conditions, the baseline collapses in 3/3 seeds while our approach remains stable in 3/3 seeds, with a 1400x reduction in KL divergence.

self_declared_provenance.quote: ECHO-2 (Xiao et al., 2026) introduces a staleness budget mechanism to tolerate slow workers in heterogeneous clusters, but couples the publication period with the staleness budget, limiting scalability... Our work identifies that the coupling between publication period and staleness budget is the root cause of training instability, and proposes decoupling them via sparse patch dissemination.
Our sparse patch dissemination builds on these insights, achieving 12.5x compression for single-step weight deltas to enable per-step publication.

Unlike these algorithmic approaches that modify the optimization objective, our work addresses stability through the system design by decoupling publication frequency from staleness tolerance, keeping rollouts near-on-policy regardless of the staleness budget.
